entry.title: VirtIO
entry.summary: This article introduces the basic concepts and core architecture of VirtIO (Virtual Input/Output). VirtIO is an abstraction layer between virtual machines and host devices, achieving data transmission through minimal VirtIO devices, offloading most hardware processing work to the host, thereby improving efficiency. The article elaborates on three key components of the VirtIO architecture: the front-end driver (kernel modules in the Guest kernel), the back-end device (such as VirtIO devices in QEMU), and VirtQueues/VRings. Among them, VRing is the actual data structure, with the classic layout being the split ring, consisting of three contiguous memory areas: the descriptor table, the available ring, and the used ring, utilizing a lock-free SPSC mechanism to achieve data sharing and notification between the driver and the device. The article also mentions the standardization significance of the VirtIO specification, as well as the flexibility in different implementations (such as the Linux kernel and OpenAMP).

entry.title: open-gpu-kernel-modules compilation
entry.summary: This article introduces the compilation method for NVIDIA open-gpu-kernel-modules, focusing on the steps and key parameters for cross-compilation using the ARM GNU toolchain, including the distinction between ARCH=arm64 and TARGET_ARCH=aarch64, toolchain path configuration, and cleanup methods. The article also summarizes the two-layer build model of the repository: an OS-independent core (src) combined with a Linux kernel adaptation layer (kernel-open), ultimately producing 5 kernel modules. It further outlines the functionality of each module, code distribution, and the central role of GSP firmware in the architecture's evolution.

entry.title: OpenSSL 1.0.0s aarch64 cross-compilation
entry.summary: This article introduces the complete process of cross-compiling OpenSSL 1.0.0s on an x86_64 host using the Arm GNU Toolchain 11.2 to generate aarch64 shared libraries (.so). The article first explains the environment preparation, including source code selection and cross-toolchain configuration, and points out that OpenSSL 1.0.0 does not have a dedicated aarch64 target, so a generic 64-bit target must be used with the toolchain prefix specified via environment variables. It then provides a detailed analysis of the Configure parameters, including disabling the IDEA, MD2, MDC2, and RC5 algorithms as well as the SSL 2.0/3.0 protocols, and explains the related security considerations. The article focuses on solving a key issue in the build process: because the cross-toolchain's `ar` defaults to creating thin archives when ARFLAGS is empty, and the AR parameter order is incorrect, leading to link failures, it is necessary to modify the ARFLAGS and AR definitions in the top-level Makefile, Makefile, and Makefile.shared simultaneously. Finally, it summarizes the compilation, verification, and installation steps, and provides a troubleshooting table for common issues. This article provides a reference for the ARM64 platform

entry.title: Tag Plugin Plus External Tags Overview
entry.summary: This article introduces the comprehensive features of the Tag Plugin Plus plugin tag, systematically testing the current theme's rendering support for standard Markdown and extended syntax. The article covers a wealth of content including heading levels, inline formatting (bold, italic, strikethrough, highlight, superscript/subscript), links, images, lists (unordered, ordered, task lists), blockquotes, code blocks, tables (including cell merging), horizontal rules, footnotes, Emoji, escape characters, mathematical formulas (KaTeX), and Mermaid diagrams. It focuses on demonstrating horizontal and vertical table cell merging, combined merging, and edge cases, and verifies the actual rendering effects of mathematical formulas and Mermaid diagrams, helping users fully understand the extent of the theme's support for Markdown syntax.

entry.title: Remoteproc resource table
entry.summary: This article introduces the concept and implementation of the Remoteproc resource table. Remote processor firmware images typically contain a resource table, user applications, an RTOS or bare-metal code, and the OpenAMP library. The resource table is used to describe the system resources required by the remote processor (such as contiguous physical memory and peripherals) as well as the configuration of the Virtio devices it supports (such as vring addresses and sizes). The article provides a detailed analysis of the struct resource_table structure and the resource entry header fw_rsc_hdr, and explains how the Remoteproc framework locates and registers Virtio devices via the resource table. Finally, taking the STM32MP15C as an example, it introduces the specific implementation of the rsc_table, including the definition of the resource table, the initialization process, and its coordination with the reserved-memory node in the device tree.

entry.title: OpenAMP
entry.summary: This article introduces the OpenAMP (Open Asymmetric Multiprocessing) software framework, developed by Mentor Graphics and Xilinx, which addresses communication issues between RTOS or bare-metal programs and Linux in AMP systems. The article elaborates on the core components of OpenAMP: Virtio provides a virtual device framework for shared memory management, enabling data transfer through vring ring buffers; RPMsg acts as a Virtio-based message bus, responsible for inter-core message communication; and Remoteproc is used for the lifecycle management of remote processors, including firmware loading, startup/shutdown, and resource parsing. Taking the STM32MP157 as an example, the article explains the communication mechanism between Cortex-A7 and Cortex-M4 via OpenAMP, and compares the differences between the Linux-side and bare-metal-side underlying drivers.

entry.title: IPCC
entry.summary: This article introduces Inter-Process Communication (IPC) and its hardware controller IPCC, focusing on the STM32MP157 as an example. It elaborates on the working modes (simplex, half-duplex, full-duplex) of the IPCC's 6 bidirectional channels (12 sub-channels) and their specific uses in the official ST configuration, including channels 1 and 2 used for the RPMsg framework to implement message transmission between the A7 and M4 cores, and channel 3 used for the RemoteProc framework to control the coprocessor lifecycle. The article also explains that the IPCC only provides an interrupt notification mechanism, while actual data is transmitted through shared memory, and introduces the related 8 registers and the interrupt control for each of the two processors. Additionally, it mentions the integration of the OpenAMP framework on the Linux side and the M4 side.

entry.title: Rpmsg Char Driver
entry.summary: This paper introduces the design and implementation of the Rpmsg character device driver in Linux 5.10.x. The driver registers to the Rpmsg bus and adopts a mode that separates control devices from endpoint devices: the control node creates endpoints via ioctl, and the endpoint devices handle user-space message reading and writing. The article analyzes key data structures, the use of locks and wait queues, the probe/remove flow, the deferred creation mechanism of endpoints, as well as details in the read/write paths such as blocking wakeup and memory copy, and points out considerations such as buffer size.

entry.title: Rpmsg Core
entry.summary: This article introduces the design and implementation of the rpmsg core in the Linux kernel. As a bus abstraction, rpmsg is not tied to any specific transport and can support various backend implementations based on shared memory, mailbox interrupts, or PCIe doorbells. Each backend only needs to provide the corresponding operations to interface with the core. The article elaborates on the rpmsg device matching mechanism (rpmsg_dev_match) priority scoring rules, which calculate scores by comparing specific/general driver constraints, compat matching, and of_node matching and other conditions to determine the optimal driver. Meanwhile, the article summarizes the rpmsg device probe flow (rpmsg_dev_probe), including key steps such as power domain association (genpd), automatic endpoint creation, and calling the driver probe function, and explains the mechanism of dynamic endpoint address allocation and callback binding.

entry.title: Virtio Rpmsg Bus
entry.summary: This article introduces the virtio-based rpmsg bus driver in the Linux kernel (virtio_rpmsg_bus), elaborating on its role as the virtio transport implementation for the rpmsg bus, responsible for sending and receiving messages between the Linux main core and the remote processor via vring, and abstracting remote services as rpmsg_devices for upper-layer driver binding. The article analyzes in detail the three-layer structure of rpmsg, the communication model, and core data structures such as rpmsg_device、rpmsg_endpoint and virtproc_info, and explains key mechanisms such as endpoint creation and destruction, buffer management, send synchronization, and name service. Finally, it points out that rpmsg is actually an address-based message distribution mechanism.

entry.title: Commonly Used Data Structures in the Linux Kernel
entry.summary: This article introduces common general-purpose data structures in the Linux kernel, sorting them by actual usage frequency from high to low, starting with the doubly linked circular list `list`_head, hash linked list `hlist`, red-black tree `rbtree`, radix tree `radix`_`tree` and other core structures, covering their data structure definitions, core APIs, and typical use cases. The article is based on the Linux 6.x kernel and has synchronously updated loadable module examples for each data structure, making it easier for developers to understand and apply them.

entry.title: ClaudeCode
entry.summary: This article introduces the installation and configuration methods for Claude Code, including Node.js environment requirements, the reasons for choosing DeepSeek as the API provider and the application process, as well as integration steps for VSCode and Emacs editors and environment variable configuration methods. The article also explains the Skill extension mechanism in detail—the skill packages launched by Anthropic in October 2025, which are essentially Markdown files, with two storage locations: project-level directories and user-level directories. It also introduces the concept of MCP (Model Context Protocol) and its role. Finally, the article recommends several practical Skills, such as Karpathy-Inspired Claude Code Guidelines, codegraph, draw.io, and CC-Switch, and explains two methods for installing Skills.

entry.title: smatch
entry.summary: This article introduces Smatch, a static analysis tool specifically designed for the Linux kernel, capable of deeply tracking code execution paths to discover deep-seated defects such as null pointer dereferences, lock usage errors, and resource leaks. The article details Smatch's compilation method, database construction process, and its cross-file vulnerability detection capabilities, and provides script parameter and output file descriptions for running Smatch to check the entire kernel or specified files/folders, while also mentioning the analysis method for out-of-tree modules and the configuration of the smatch_data rules directory.

entry.title: Query the earliest introduced version of a kernel API
entry.summary: This article introduces the method to query the earliest version in which a kernel API was introduced, and illustrates it with a specific API as an example.
